subject: Archive eviction schedule & escrowed-snapshot handling for Mediconnect
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@mediconnect.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@mediconnect.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Snapshot eviction & cross-border flag questions

Laura — thanks for taking this on. A few items we need clarified before Procurement can sign the DPA amendments: 

1) Backups and immutable snapshots: Are customer snapshots for Mediconnect placed outside of our requested region (we asked for us-central1) during routine cross-zone replication? We need the subprocessor list for any provider storing snapshots.

2) Deletion workflow: When we submit an erasure request under our DSRs, what is the orchestration timeline to remove (a) active records, (b) cached indexes / embeddings, and (c) snapshot copies that may be on longer-term retention? We understand some snapshot media may be immutable for a limited window — please give a concrete eviction schedule.

3) Evidence: Will Redwood provide a final deletion attestation and a log of the orchestration run (job id + timestamps)? We will need an auditable proof-of-deletion for our regulators.

Attached: current DPA redline from Legal and a short matrix describing where Mediconnect’s data lives today.

Appreciate a proposed timetable and any recommended DPA language for escrowed snapshots / backups.

— Alex
Compliance, Mediconnect
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@mediconnect.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot eviction & cross-border flag questions

Alex — thanks, and apologies for the length; trying to be concrete so Procurement/Legal have actionable items. Draft answers below and proposed changes to the DPA. See attached policy matrix for mapping of store type -> location -> TTL.

1) Snapshot placement: Primary copies are pinned to the customer region (us-central1). We do perform cross-zone replication for durability; however, we do not proactively copy customer snapshots to other regions unless the customer enables cross-region replication. Subprocessors that may hold encrypted copies for disaster recovery are listed on the subprocessor registry; for Mediconnect’s profile those are (example): GCP (us-central1), FastArchive Inc. (us-west-backup). We will update the subprocessor notification scope in the DPA amendment to include any ephemeral DR replica stores.

2) Deletion workflow & eviction windows: Proposal: for snapshots created by the runtime, apply a two-stage eviction: 
  - Quarantine window (30 days): upon customer erasure request we mark snapshots as quarantined and remove read access; they are retained but isolated for 30 days to allow restore/rollback requests.
  - Eviction window (90 days after quarantine start, i.e., 120 days total maximum from request): immutable on-tape style copies are scheduled for secure wipe during the eviction job.

Rationale: we can honor on-demand purge requests for active+cache layers within 24–72 hours; immutable media that sits in long-term DR stores often requires coordinated wipe jobs with third-party subprocessors which is why we surface the 120-day maximum. If Mediconnect requires a faster hard guarantee, we can add a carveout in the DPA with an escrowed-snapshot exception (see point 3).

3) Proof-of-deletion & attestations: We will provide a signed deletion attestation, plus the orchestration log (job id, start/end time, subprocessor ack receipts where available). For escrowed-snapshot exceptions (customer funds a disposable escrow rotation or special retainer), we can contract a shorter quarantine (for example 30 days total) but this requires an addendum covering certs and audit access.

Next steps I recommend: 
  - Kimberly: review legal language for the escrowed-snapshot carveout.
  - Marcus: confirm the operational runbook for eviction jobs and the expected subprocessor ack cadence.
  - Alex: confirm whether Mediconnect can accept the 120-day max for immutable media or if you need a commercial addendum now.

Attachments: mediconnect_dpa_redline_v2.pdf, snapshot_policy_matrix.xlsx

Thanks — Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Risk & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot eviction & cross-border flag questions

Team — quick legal read: the proposed two-stage model is reasonable operationally, but Legal cannot commit Redwood to immediate destruction of data stored on immutable third-party media without contractual indemnities. A few suggestions to capture in the DPA amendment: 

- Escrowed-snapshot exception: If Mediconnect requires <30-day> final wipe, we should add an explicit addendum that: (a) enumerates the covered snapshot IDs, (b) requires Mediconnect-funded secure-wipe runs (to cover subprocessor costs), and (c) includes an attestation timeline (we recommend 10 business days post-wipe for Redwood attestation).

- Subprocessor notification: Add a clause requiring Redwood to notify Mediconnect within 7 business days of any intended subprocessor change that could materially affect snapshot placement or retention.

- Audit logs exception: we can accept a limited exception where security logs are retained up to 12 months for incident response, but those logs must be redacted for PII and segregated; include this as a separate schedule in the DPA.

I’ve added markup to mediconnect_dpa_redline_v2.pdf and pushed a DocuSign route for the amendment that includes the escrow addendum as an optional exhibit. Link: https://www.docusign.com/signed/XYZ-7462

—Kimberly
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@mediconnect.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@mediconnect.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Snapshot eviction & cross-border flag questions

Laura/Kimberly — thanks for the clear options. Mediconnect is comfortable with the two-stage model for standard accounts. A couple of follow-ups: 

• We need the attestation SLA to be spelled out in the DocuSign amendment (we accept Kimberly’s 10 business days post-wipe).
• For security logs: Mediconnect can accept 12-month retention for redacted incident-response logs; please provide the redaction and segregation controls that will be used.
• Please confirm the orchestration job id format so we can reference it in our ticketing system (we'd like job id + subprocessor ack hash).

If you can route the amended DPA with Kimberly’s escrow exhibit and the attestation SLA, Procurement can sign once the DocuSign is updated.

— Alex
Compliance, Mediconnect
